chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Sadan ibn ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked him: 'Is there a fixed time for this matter (the reappearance), so that we can rest our bodies and wait for it?' He replied: 'Yes, but you publicized it, so God increased it (postponed it).'

key_terms.أَمَدٌّ: A fixed time, period, or limit
key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter, specifically referring to the reappearance (al-Zuhur) of the Imam (a.s)

ai.seo_question: What is the reason for the postponement of the Imam's reappearance according to Hadith 9 of Kitab al-Ghayba?
ai.summary: Abu Basir inquires whether the Imam’s reappearance has a fixed, calculable timeframe allowing for passive waiting, to which the Imam affirms its certainty. He adds a crucial nuance: the 'extension' of the time is a divine response to the companions' premature publicization of the knowledge, illustrating the dynamic interplay between human action and divine decree in Shia eschatology. This highlights that while the event is inevitable, its timing is not static but responsive to the community's spiritual readiness and conduct.
